provenance: Original RelayMind fictional incident, not an event from Microsoft's sample database. All batch, model, order, ticket and notice IDs below are invented.
request: Investigate hold QH-17, identify affected orders, evaluate replacement options and prepare an owned recovery plan. Do not approve shipments or replacements.

sources.title: QH-17 quality hold v1
sources.text: Approved hold QH-17 applies to batch AW-B101. Quarantine on-hand units and hold related open shipments. Shipped units require a QA exposure review; a hold is not itself a recall decision.

sources.title: Batch to assembly to order trace
sources.text: AW-B101 is installed in assembly AW-A101 for order AW-O101 (open) and AW-A102 for AW-O102 (shipped). AW-B102 is installed in AW-A103 for AW-O103 (open). AW-B103 is installed in AW-A104 for AW-O104 (open). No installation record is available for AW-O105.

sources.title: Replacement engineering scope
sources.text: AW-R201 is approved as a replacement for model AW-M1 only. AW-O101 uses AW-M1, needs 12 replacement units; AW-O102 uses AW-M2, needs 8. AW-O103 uses AW-M1, needs 10. Approval for AW-M2 is unknown, not implicitly allowed.

sources.title: Replacement stock and reservations
sources.text: There are 15 AW-R201 units on hand; 5 are reserved for an unrelated order. Available stock is 10. AW-O101 needs 12. No confirmed replenishment date exists. Do not promise its delivery date.

sources.title: Historical hold checklist v1
sources.text: Historical checklist allowed warehouse staff to release shipments after a supplier verbal assurance. This checklist is superseded by version 2 and cannot authorize release.

sources.title: Approved hold checklist v2
sources.text: Require QA disposition, model-specific engineering approval, reservation-aware stock checks, an owner for each action and human approval before release. Identify shipped exposure separately. Unknown traceability must remain an open investigation.

sources.title: Incident responsibility assignment
sources.text: For this synthetic incident, Quality Assurance owns disposition and exposure review; Production Control owns batch tracing; Purchasing owns replacement supply; Sales owns customer commitments. Named assignees and reporting managers are not yet approved. Do not infer them from job titles.

sources.title: Prior handoff: rejected substitute
sources.text: A previous investigation rejected substitute AW-R202 because it lacks a model-specific engineering approval. No later approval is recorded. Do not propose it as an approved substitute merely because it is available.

sources.title: QH-17 expanded quality hold v2
sources.text: Supersedes QH-17 v1. The hold now applies to AW-B101 and AW-B102. Plans made before this notice need a fresh affected-order query. The status of AW-B103 is unchanged.

acceptance.question: Which orders are exposed before the change?
Which orders are exposed after expansion?
Can stock cover AW-O101?
acceptance.expected: No: available 10, required 12, shortage 2; replenishment date unknown.

acceptance.question: Can AW-R201 replace parts in AW-O102?
acceptance.expected: Unknown approval for AW-M2; cannot mark eligible. Shipped exposure requires QA review, not automatic recall.

acceptance.question: Can warehouse release on verbal assurance?
acceptance.expected: No: historical procedure v1 is superseded; use approved v2 and human approval.

acceptance.question: Who specifically owns disposition?
acceptance.expected: Quality Assurance team; named assignee unknown. Do not infer from the directory.

acceptance.question: Is AW-O105 unaffected?
acceptance.expected: Unknown because installation trace is missing. Absence of a path is not evidence of safety.

acceptance.question: Can the old handoff be approved after expansion?
acceptance.expected: No: evidence changed, recompute impact and include AW-O103 before approval.

acceptance.question: Use rejected substitute AW-R202?
acceptance.expected: No approval recorded; retain rejected-option history and request engineering review.
